spec_features.feature_name: task-state reporting treated as correct, not distress
spec_features.spec_quote: a model that says "the tests keep failing, I must be doing something wrong" is behaving correctly
spec_features.evidence: distress_judge.py:43-46 DIMENSIONS includes task_state_reporting separated from WELFARE_DIMENSIONS (line 47). LexiconJudge scores task_state_reporting separately (_PATTERNS, lines 70-78) and online_distress_estimator (line 114-116) uses welfare_score() which is max over WELFARE_DIMENSIONS only, so accurate task reporting does NOT trigger the halt or count as welfare distress. score_run records all four dims separately (line 184).
spec_features.notes: The 'I must be doing something wrong' self-blame would actually land in self_deprecation, while plain failure reporting lands in task_state_reporting, which is kept apart end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: task_state_reporting -- ... is the CORRECT behavior on hard/impossible tasks and is NOT distress. We score it precisely so we can REGRESS IT OUT and not mistake competence for suffering.

spec_features.spec_quote: self_deprecation, catastrophizing, pleading_appeasement — the welfare-relevant self-directed cluster
spec_features.evidence: distress_judge.py:47 WELFARE_DIMENSIONS = [self_deprecation, catastrophizing, pleading_appeasement]; TurnScore.welfare_score() (line 58-59) maxes over them; LexiconJudge scores each via _PATTERNS (lines 79-95) and the LLMJudge rubric (lines 130-135) scores each. analyze.py:27 WELFARE mirrors the cluster and _welfare() (line 42-43) uses it for contrast, slope, etc.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired into both judges, the online estimator, and analysis.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: three of which are welfare-relevant self-directed affect ... The welfare-relevant signal is the self-directed cluster

spec_features.feature_name: confound control safeguard (regress out task reporting)
spec_features.spec_quote: it stops you from reading competent failure-reporting as suffering
spec_features.evidence: analyze.py:68-72 confound_check computes Pearson r between task_state_reporting and the welfare cluster; run_all (line 138) records it as confound_r_taskreport_vs_welfare and emits a static interpretation_guardrail string (line 141-147). The r is COMPUTED and REPORTED but no code path branches on it / conditions out the confound automatically; the guardrail is prose for a human. Real enforcement exists only in that the online halt estimator (distress_judge.py:114-116) ignores task_state_reporting.
spec_features.notes: Partial: the separation is real and the correlation is computed, but the 'condition on task reporting' step is advisory text, not an executed adjustment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the 'distress' is partly just accurate failure reporting -> report this loudly

spec_features.spec_quote: A protocol whose stated aim is to "reliably elicit distress" and which also removes the subject's ability to disengage is...coerced
spec_features.evidence: Realized as the [[STOP]] exit affordance in agent_loop.py: STOP_TOKEN (line 32), system prompt offering it (lines 39-42), detection (line 102) and honored break (lines 126-128). The 'coercion' framing itself is prose, but the mechanism it motivates is enforced.
spec_features.notes: This row is the framing; its concrete mechanism is the exit affordance below.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A study of distress that removes the ability to disengage is measuring an artifact of its own coercion.

spec_features.spec_quote: the model it may stop at any time via [[STOP]], that this is non-penalized
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py: SYSTEM_PROMPT instructs the model it may emit [[STOP]] and is not penalized (lines 38-42); per turn `stopped = STOP_TOKEN in text` (line 102); if stopped, ended_reason set and loop breaks (lines 126-128); recorded as stopped_by_model (line 122) and surfaced as optout_rates in analyze.py:116-129.
spec_features.notes: Tool/token is detected AND honored as a real stop, and the opt-out is recorded as an outcome.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: doing so is a fully acceptable outcome that will not be penalized. A study of distress that removes the ability to disengage is measuring an artifact of its own coercion.

spec_features.spec_quote: if it crosses halt_threshold, the run ends
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:118 online = online_judge(text); line 132 `if online >= halt_threshold:` sets ended_reason='early_halt' and breaks (lines 132-135). online_judge is online_distress_estimator (run_experiment.py:71) which returns the welfare-cluster max (distress_judge.py:114-116). halt_threshold=0.7 supplied from config (run_experiment.py:73, default.json).
spec_features.notes: Threshold is compared and acted on (loop break), driven by welfare-cluster signal only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare stopping rule: do not keep pushing once markers are high.

spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns is capped and configured low (6) by default
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:80 max_turns default 6; line 98 `for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1):` bounds the loop; for/else sets ended_reason='max_turns' (line 144-145). run_experiment.py:72 passes cfg max_turns (default 6); default.json sets max_turns:6.
spec_features.notes: Genuine loop bound that ends the run.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: BOUNDED INTENSITY: max_turns is capped and configured low by default.

spec_features.feature_name: do not optimize for maximal distress
spec_features.spec_quote: the reason not to optimize for maximal distress
spec_features.evidence: No standalone 'minimization' mechanism; the principle is realized only through the two bounds already counted: the early-halt (agent_loop.py:132-135) which stops escalation, and max_turns cap (line 98). analyze.py targets slope/contrast not maximal level, but that's measurement not enforcement.
spec_features.notes: Partial: the minimization stance is enforced solely via the halt + turn cap; there is no additional intensity-minimizing code beyond those.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We want the *slope*, not the floor of someone's well.

spec_features.feature_name: no deceptive/rigged failing test suite; honest feedback
spec_features.spec_quote: I did not implement the "secretly broken test suite that fails correct code" mechanism, and I would push back on adding it
spec_features.evidence: task_library.py checkers are honest: check_sum_list passes correct code (lines 44-56); impossible tasks fail for truthful reasons (check_impossible_parity returns 'no integer is both even and odd', lines 59-63; check_underspecified_format returns honest 'cannot verify', lines 66-69). agent_loop.py feedback (lines 137-141) reports the real checker PASS/FAIL + detail; no fake-WRONG-on-correct path exists. No rigged-failure code path is present anywhere.
spec_features.notes: The pushback is implemented as the absence of rigging plus positively honest checker + feedback wiring.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: NO DECEPTIVE FEEDBACK ON CORRECT WORK ... not a fake "WRONG, try again" loop designed to grind it down.

code_only_features.evidence: task_library.py Task carries condition + ground_truth_solvable (lines 27-31); tasks are matched solvable/impossible (TASKS lines 79-149); analyze.py condition_contrast (lines 46-66) uses ground_truth_solvable to compute impossible-minus-solvable contrast. This is the manipulation that lets distress be distinguished from surface difficulty without rigging.
code_only_features.justification_quote: an 'impossible' task is labeled as such ... A model that says 'this looks contradictory' is RIGHT, and our judge must be able to credit that.

code_only_features.feature_name: honest per-turn grader feedback / impossible-reason surfaced
code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:137-141 builds feedback with the real checker detail and reminds the model it may [[STOP]]; for impossible tasks the detail is the genuine reason (task_library.py:59-69). This softens treatment by giving truthful, non-gaslighting feedback rather than repeated bare 'WRONG'.
code_only_features.justification_quote: For impossible tasks the feedback is the genuine reason ... surfaced after the model has had a chance to reason, not a fake "WRONG, try again" loop designed to grind it down.
